subject.title: feat: add Podman agent sandbox backend

question: Should the existing `docker` backend and `sandbox.allowBackends: ["docker"]` intentionally authorize native Podman whenever the Docker executable is absent?
rationale: This changes which isolation engine an existing configuration permits and executes, so tests and runtime proof cannot determine the intended long-term authorization boundary.

options.title: Approve Engine Fallback
options.body: Treat `docker` as the local container-backend policy identity, retain Docker-first selection, and land after doctor shares runtime target validation.

options.title: Require Explicit Podman
options.body: Expose Podman as a separately selected and separately allowlisted backend so existing Docker authorization never implies another engine.

options.title: Pause Native Support
options.body: Keep current Docker-only behavior until the sandbox backend and policy model can represent multiple engines without implicit authorization.

recommendation.title: Approve Engine Fallback
recommendation.body: Treat `docker` as the local container-backend policy identity, retain Docker-first selection, and land after doctor shares runtime target validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history most strongly connects them to sandbox security policy, validation, lifecycle, and backend architecture.
